doc.title: Tom Varner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 13, 2025

title: How he titles pieces
summary: Titles sometimes come after listening to free improvisations, sometimes during composing.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: At what point do you assign a title to your work?

Sometimes that’s hard, especially all these crazy miniatures of the last fall. It’s only on Band Camp so I’ll be happy to send you codes for those more recent ones. But sometimes it’s after the fact. I’ll listen and I’ll go, “Okay this should be the title for this – this should be the title for that.” Sometimes I’m really working on the piece if it’s more of a written music piece, I’m on the piano and I’m sweating it out, I will already know the title. I
think it just depends on the situation. If it’s very much a free improv usually the title comes afterwards. I’m trying to think, what about – yeah, something like that.
